best_for: Electronics hobbyists, students and small hardware teams who design their own circuit boards and want a full schematic-to-PCB suite with no license fees.
description:
KiCad is a suite for designing electronic circuits and printed circuit boards. Jean-Pierre Charras first released it in 1992, and today the KiCad Development Team runs it, led by Wayne Stambaugh. The project says it aims at professional designers while keeping the hard parts out of a beginner's way.

You can draw your own symbols when the library lacks a part, and an electrical rules checker catches wiring mistakes before layout. When the board is done, export Gerber or IPC-2581 files to send to a board maker, and open Gerber files in the built-in viewer to check them first. A technical committee of the lead developers makes most decisions by consensus.

points.title: Free for good
points.text: KiCad is open source under the GPL, and the project calls the whole suite forever free. Hobby boards and commercial products use the same download.

points.title: Schematic to finished board
points.text: Draw hierarchical schematics with hundreds of sheets, lay out the board with an interactive router, and check mechanical fit in a 3D viewer with a raytracer.

points.title: Simulate before you order
points.text: A SPICE simulator is built in, so you can test parts of a circuit before paying for boards.

points.title: Big libraries, big download
points.text: The official libraries hold thousands of symbols. That has a cost: the Flathub build is about 600 MB to download and over 1.2 GB installed.

points.title: System versions
points.text: KiCad 10 supports Windows 10 and 11 on x64 and Arm64, and macOS 12 or later with one universal build. The Windows installer can install per-user or for all users.

points.title: Linux: AppImage or Flatpak
points.text: KiCad's own Linux download is an AppImage, in Full and Lite builds. The Flathub build is published by the KiCad developers and marked verified. The Windows listing keeps 55 versions; macOS and Linux list only the current release.
